products.name: Chroma
products.note: Open-source embedding database; local-first; lightweight RAG; self-hosted option

reading.body:
Chroma provides open-source embedding infrastructure licensed under Apache 2.0, positioning security and compliance as core design choices rather than add-ons for enterprises.

The company's architecture centers on local-first deployment and self-hosting, which means compute stays on customer infrastructure rather than flowing through centralized servers. This matters for AI workloads because embedding databases are critical middleware in retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, where data locality and network overhead directly affect latency and throughput. By building for lightweight, self-hosted use, Chroma reduces the external compute and bandwidth requirements that would otherwise flow to cloud providers.

The data shows only the product category and licensing model. It does not cover deployment scale, customer base, infrastructure costs, or whether enterprises actually choose self-hosting or opt for managed services that would increase centralized compute demand. profile_text.body:
Chroma describes itself as open-source search infrastructure for AI. On its own site, the company says it brings the security, compliance, education and operational model that enterprises need, built on an Apache 2.0 architecture.

The company's product is also named Chroma. It is described as an open-source embedding database that is local-first, aimed at lightweight RAG, and available as a self-hosted option.
